perceptual-cognitive behavior is self-organized in a way such that the emergence or disappearance of a perceptual-cognitive mode can be described as a critical phenomenon of a self-organizing system.
(a) perceptual-cognitive modes are conceptualized as self-organizing states of the nervous system, and that (b) response times can exhibit a peaked shape close to mode-mode transitions.

the question of how perceptual-cognitive modes emerge and are maintained in the face of environmental and task demands, and how this process relates to behavioral responses.

peaked response time curves are not necessarily an indicator of the mode-mode transition, but rather an indicator of the interaction between order-parameter and adaptation dynamics.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perceptual-cognitive behavioral modes can be conceptualized as order parameters of a self-organization process.
perceptual-cognitive behavior is a self-organizing phenomenon that is characterized by the emergence of behavioral modes.

the order parameter concept and the concept of system parameter dynamics provide a framework that can account for the emergence of behavioral modes, for hysteresis, for response time curves with a peak close to mode-mode-transition points, and for response time curves exhibiting a plateau.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the order parameter model provides a framework that allows for a unified treatment of perceptual-cognition-behavioral phenomena such as mode-mode transitions and response times in a way that is consistent with the theory of selforganization.
a model-based approach is needed to understand perceptual-cognitive behavioral mode-mode transitions.

the two-component order parameter/system parameter model can account for a wide variety of perceptual-cognition-behavioral effects in the context of perceptual judgment tasks, and that it is worthwhile to consider the emergence of perceptuo-cognitive-behavioural modes as a critical phenomenon.
